questions.question: A company is designing an internal workshop-planning agent. It must understand the workshop goal, remember participant count and preferred date, check venue availability, create schedules and documents, send invitations, react if the venue becomes unavailable, and require a manager to approve major changes. Which architecture most completely reflects Module 3?

options.A: A reasoning model supported by appropriate memory and tools, operating through Plan - Act - Observe while retaining human oversight for important decisions
options.B: A chatbot with a detailed persona that generates all outputs in a single response and performs no external actions
options.C: A knowledge base containing workshop documents but no reasoning component, tools or review process
options.D: A calendar automation that follows a fixed sequence regardless of new information or failed actions

questions.question: A project team compares two setups. Setup X is a reusable role-specific assistant for recurring tasks. Setup Y is a workspace where many conversations inherit shared project instructions and uploaded project knowledge. Which distinction is most consistent with the module?

options.A: X resembles an assistant-based configuration; Y resembles Claude's project-based workspace.
options.B: X must be Claude Projects; Y must be a Gemini Gem.
options.C: Both are identical because every no-code AI product shares context in exactly the same way.
options.D: Y represents a newly trained model while X represents prompt engineering.

questions.question: A newly configured Gem works perfectly for the exact example used during setup. What is the strongest next validation step?

options.A: Save it immediately because one successful response proves consistency.
options.B: Test only the same prompt repeatedly until the wording becomes identical.
options.C: Replace its instructions with a shorter version without comparing results.
options.D: Give it different but related requests and check whether the configured behavior remains consistent.

questions.question: A manager tells an agent, “Send the final report to our usual executive distribution list.” The agent knows how to send email but does not know which executives belong to the usual list. What is the main missing capability?

options.A: Another email tool
options.B: A stronger language model
options.C: A document-editing capability
options.D: Relevant remembered or stored information about the recipients

questions.question: An agent sends a calendar invitation. Which activity represents the Observe stage rather than Plan or Act?

options.A: Checking whether the invitation was successfully created and accepted
options.B: Deciding that a meeting is necessary
options.C: Selecting the calendar tool
options.D: Writing the invitation description

questions.question: A reusable assistant already has clear instructions and reference documents. The team now enables a connection that allows it to schedule meetings rather than merely suggest meeting times. What role does this new configuration primarily play?

options.A: It replaces the model's reasoning.
options.B: It gives the assistant an external action capability.
options.C: It creates semantic memory about scheduling.
options.D: It turns the assistant into a newly trained AI model.

questions.question: A consulting team works on the same policy-development project for six months. They want every new conversation in the workspace to inherit project instructions, uploaded knowledge and shared context. Which module platform is most directly designed around this pattern?

options.A: Claude Projects
options.B: A standard one-off chatbot conversation
options.C: Gemini Gems only
options.D: An unconfigured general-purpose chat

questions.question: A finance agent prepares a recommendation affecting a major investment. It has analyzed documents, used calculation tools and produced a detailed rationale. What does the module still recommend?

options.A: A qualified human should review the important decision before implementation.
options.B: The agent should automatically execute because multiple tools were used.
options.C: The result requires no review once memory and tools agree.
options.D: Human involvement should be limited to correcting grammar.

questions.question: An executive argues, “The agent checked its memory, used the correct tools and produced a confident recommendation. Therefore human review would add no value.” Which response most closely reflects the module?

options.A: Correct, the three building blocks remove the need for human judgment.
options.B: Correct, but only when episodic memory is available.
options.C: Incorrect only if the agent has fewer than three external tools.
options.D: Important decisions can still require human context, ethical judgment and accountability.

questions.question: In the Module 3 workshop, trainees perform the same task using a configured Gemini Gem and a normal Gemini chat. What observation would provide the strongest evidence that reusable configuration is working as intended?

options.A: The Gem maintains the intended role, formatting and rules across related prompts with less repeated instruction.
options.B: The Gem always produces a longer response than normal chat.
options.C: The standard chat stops understanding the task completely.
options.D: The Gem gives the same exact wording every time regardless of the request.

questions.question: A travel assistant receives the goal: “Plan my three-day Pokhara trip within NPR 40,000.” It compares options, builds an itinerary, checks whether the selected activities fit the budget, changes one hotel when the cost becomes too high, and then presents the completed plan. Which characteristic most strongly separates this behavior from a traditional chatbot?

options.A: It produces several paragraphs instead of a single answer.
options.B: It remembers that Pokhara is a travel destination.
options.C: It uses natural language rather than a fixed menu.
options.D: It determines and adjusts the steps needed to accomplish the goal.

questions.question: A meeting agent remembers that Room A was available every Monday for the past month. Today, the live booking tool reports that Room A is occupied. What should a well-designed agent prioritize?

options.A: The remembered pattern, because memory should override a tool after enough past observations.
options.B: The model's original plan, because changing plans reduces agent consistency.
options.C: The current observation and then replanning based on the new information.
options.D: The remembered information and tool result equally, even if they directly contradict each other.

questions.question: A support agent stores “Customer prefers email communication” and “On March 8, the customer's delivery failed and a replacement shipment resolved the case.” An engineer proposes storing both pieces of information as the same type of memory simply because both survive across sessions. What is the better analysis?

options.A: Both should be procedural because the information may influence future actions.
options.B: Both should be semantic because neither belongs to the current conversation.
options.C: The preference can be long-term user memory while the specific past case is episodic memory.
options.D: The past event should be short-term while the preference should be semantic.

questions.question: A customer-support agent is being designed to improve over time. The team wants it to remember useful customer preferences, how previous unusual support incidents were resolved, and the company's standard refund workflow. Which combination is most appropriate?

options.A: Long-term, episodic and procedural memory
options.B: Short-term, semantic and episodic memory
options.C: Procedural, short-term and long-term memory
options.D: Semantic, procedural and short-term memory

questions.question: An agent has access to the correct customer database, remembers the customer's previous complaint, and can send email. However, after reading the complaint it repeatedly chooses an irrelevant action even though all required information is available. Which component should be investigated first?

options.A: The model's reasoning and decision-making
options.B: The long-term memory storage mechanism
options.C: The email tool's external connection
options.D: The customer's previous interaction history

questions.question: A team creates a reusable HR assistant using an existing AI platform. They configure instructions, upload company material and enable relevant capabilities. What have they actually done?

options.A: Trained a completely new foundation model from company data
options.B: Replaced the underlying AI model with a custom neural network
options.C: Configured an existing model for a specific reusable purpose
options.D: Converted the company's documents into a new language model

questions.question: An agent preparing a workshop has already remembered the preferred date. It now needs to determine whether the venue is available and reserve it. Which sequence best reflects the architecture taught in the module?

options.A: Tool remembers the preferred date - memory evaluates alternatives - model books the venue.
options.B: Memory books the venue - model retrieves the date - calendar reasons about alternatives.
options.C: Calendar selects the best strategy - model stores the venue - memory performs the booking.
options.D: Model uses remembered preferences to decide what to check, then uses a booking/calendar tool to act.

questions.question: During a support conversation, the customer says, “My order number is 9182.” Several messages later, the agent still uses 9182 while resolving the same issue. Which memory type is most directly involved?

options.A: Semantic memory
options.B: Short-term memory
options.C: Episodic memory
options.D: Procedural memory

questions.question: An agent remembers that a previous customer accepted a 15% discount after a service failure. A new customer reports a completely different problem, but the agent automatically gives the same discount because “it worked last time.” Which conclusion is strongest?

options.A: Episodic memory should never be available to an AI agent.
options.B: Remembered past outcomes must still be interpreted appropriately for the current situation.
options.C: Procedural memory should replace the model's decision-making entirely.
options.D: Any information stored across sessions becomes a mandatory rule for future actions.

questions.question: A recruitment agent ranks applicants and recommends three candidates for final interviews. The hiring manager accepts the ranking without reviewing candidate information because “the agent already analyzed everything.” Which safeguard from the module is most clearly missing?

options.A: Human review of an important decision
options.B: Additional short-term memory
options.C: A second recruitment persona
options.D: A larger number of connected tools

questions.question: An AI application connects separately to a file service, calendar service, and internal database through MCP. Which architectural statement is most consistent with the curriculum?

options.A: One MCP Server must directly contain every external system.
options.B: A Host may manage multiple MCP clients connecting to different MCP servers.
options.C: Each AI model can use only one MCP client during its lifetime.
options.D: MCP Clients replace the AI model's reasoning component.

questions.question: A Drive-connected AI is asked, “Find the latest supplier-risk assessment.” The employee cannot remember the exact filename, but the document contains clear information about supplier risk. Which connected-AI capability is especially useful here?

options.A: Natural-language search across stored Drive content
options.B: Automatically granting the AI write access to every file
options.C: Converting every Drive document into an Artifact
options.D: Replacing the existing folder structure with a new AI-generated one before searching

questions.question: A department wants a workspace that will be reused every week. It needs consistent tone and format, internal reference materials, multiple related chats, and a report template that can be revised rather than regenerated. Which combination most directly satisfies all four needs?

options.A: A Plugin plus a browser extension only
options.B: A Skill plus separate unrelated chats
options.C: Claude Code plus one temporary conversation
options.D: A Claude Project with instructions, knowledge files, multiple chats, and a reusable Artifact

questions.question: A project has the instruction “Use a formal tone and finish every response with three action items.” The user opens a new chat inside the same Claude Project and asks an unrelated project question. Claude still follows those rules without the user repeating them. What feature is primarily responsible for this consistency?

options.A: The previous chat has been converted into an Artifact.
options.B: The Project's persistent instructions apply across its conversations.
options.C: A Plugin automatically rewrites every user message before Claude receives it.
options.D: Claude Code reads the previous chat from the local file system.

questions.question: A manager photographs a handwritten whiteboard containing tasks, arrows, and dates. They want AI to recover the visible text and explain the flow shown in the image. Which combination of capabilities is most relevant?

options.A: Excel formulas and pivot tables
options.B: Claude Project instructions and Artifacts
options.C: OCR plus visual interpretation of the image or diagram
options.D: MCP Host and Client discovery only

questions.question: A user has generated a useful calculator-like tool in Claude and expects to return later, adjust it, and reuse it rather than recreate it from a prompt each time. Why is an Artifact suitable?

options.A: Artifacts automatically provide access to any external application.
options.B: Artifacts are reusable outputs that can be edited, referenced, and iterated on.
options.C: Artifacts serve as the protocol layer between MCP Hosts and Servers.
options.D: Artifacts permanently change Claude's underlying model behavior.

questions.question: A project manager asks Claude to create a reusable weekly-status-report template. After reviewing it, the manager asks Claude to add a Risk section without regenerating the entire document from scratch. Which feature best matches this workflow?

options.A: An Artifact that can be revised and reused in place
options.B: A Skill that stores only the manager's usage statistics
options.C: A Plugin that connects to an external reporting service
options.D: A Project instruction that permanently replaces the report itself

questions.question: A manager says, “Document Intelligence is basically OCR because both can read text from documents.” Which response best reflects the curriculum?

options.A: Correct; Document Intelligence does nothing beyond converting images to text.
options.B: Correct whenever the documents contain tables.
options.C: Incomplete; Document Intelligence can understand structure and meaning, extract fields, and create structured information beyond simple text recognition.
options.D: Incorrect because OCR is used only for audio rather than documents.

questions.question: Claude analyzes an Excel workbook and proposes a chart showing a sharp increase in costs. Before management acts on the finding, an analyst discovers several rows were categorized incorrectly in the source data. What lesson is most important?

options.A: Charts generated from spreadsheets never require review.
options.B: Claude should be given full write access so it can silently correct every data problem.
options.C: Excel analysis should always be replaced by manual calculation.
options.D: AI-generated spreadsheet insights should be validated against the underlying data before important decisions.

questions.question: A document-search assistant only needs to locate and summarize files. An administrator proposes granting it permission to delete files, send emails, and change calendar events “in case those capabilities are useful later.” What principle should guide the decision?

options.A: Grant every permission because connected AI is useful only with full access.
options.B: Use write access for every integration because read-only access prevents summarization.
options.C: Apply least privilege and grant only the permissions required for the current task.
options.D: Permissions are unnecessary if the Project instructions say not to perform risky actions.

questions.question: A manager says, “The model understands that I want the latest quarterly report, so it should already be able to read the file in my Drive.” No Drive connection or file upload exists. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.A: Understanding the request automatically grants read access to all user applications.
options.B: The model still needs authorized access or a connection to retrieve information from the external system.
options.C: A sufficiently detailed prompt can replace application permissions.
options.D: The model should use procedural memory to reconstruct the missing report.

questions.question: A connected assistant must read an existing project record, update its status, and send an authorized notification after the update. Which permission concept is most likely required?

options.A: Read-only access because the AI can describe changes without making them.
options.B: Write-only access because reading is automatically included in every write scope.
options.C: No application permissions if MCP is being used.
options.D: Appropriate read-and-write permissions covering the required resources and actions.

questions.question: An AI needs to examine existing financial records but must never alter them. Which permission level most directly supports the requirement?

options.A: Read access
options.B: Write access only
options.C: Read-and-write access
options.D: Administrator access

questions.question: A team creates a Project with strong instructions but no uploaded company material. Claude follows the requested tone perfectly yet gives generic answers when asked about the company's internal procedures. What is the most direct improvement?

options.A: Increase the number of chats inside the Project.
options.B: Turn every response into an Artifact.
options.C: Add the relevant organizational documents as Project knowledge.
options.D: Install a usage-tracking browser extension.

questions.question: A claims team receives scanned accident forms. Staff need the policy number, accident date, claim amount, and damage details extracted into structured fields. Which application of Document Intelligence best matches this scenario?

options.A: Insurance document processing
options.B: Presentation generation
options.C: Project instruction management
options.D: Plugin testing

questions.question: An engineer argues that MCP is always expensive because “connecting even one tiny tool automatically consumes most of the context window.” Which evaluation is most accurate?

options.A: Correct; MCP reserves a fixed majority of the context window regardless of implementation.
options.B: Correct; every MCP server sends its entire underlying database with every request.
options.C: Incorrect only when the connected tool is a calendar.
options.D: Incorrect; token impact depends on how many tools are exposed, their definitions, returned data, and context management.

questions.question: An operations team debates whether to create a Skill or an Artifact. Their requirement is: “We need a reusable set of instructions that Claude can apply whenever it formats incident reports.” Which choice best fits the requirement?

options.A: A Skill, because the reusable asset is the task procedure Claude should follow
options.B: An Artifact, because every reusable instruction must be stored as a generated document
options.C: A Plugin, because formatting cannot be handled without an external system
options.D: A browser extension, because repeated tasks depend mainly on usage tracking

questions.question: Inside that AI application, one component establishes and maintains a communication session with a particular MCP server, discovers its capabilities, sends requests, and receives results. What is this component?

options.A: MCP Client
options.B: MCP Host
options.C: Model context window
options.D: Claude Artifact

questions.question: An organization wants an end-to-end AI workflow that retrieves approved business documents, extracts relevant information, prepares an executive summary and presentation, and updates an authorized workplace record. The documents are sensitive and some extracted values may be uncertain. Which design best reflects the combined principles of Module 4?

options.A: Give the AI unrestricted access to every connected system so the workflow never pauses for permissions.
options.B: Use AI only for generating text and manually perform every retrieval, extraction, and update because connected workflows are unsupported.
options.C: Use authorized connected tools with least-privilege access, apply Document Intelligence to the required data, validate important outputs, and retain human oversight where sensitivity or uncertainty warrants it.
options.D: Place all documents into a public Project and rely on custom instructions to prevent unauthorized use.

questions.question: A team connects 120 MCP tools to an AI assistant even though most users need only a few of them. They then notice that requests use substantially more context tokens before useful work begins. What is the strongest curriculum-based explanation?

options.A: MCP retrains the model every time a new tool becomes available.
options.B: External tools consume tokens only when they modify files.
options.C: Tool definitions, schemas, and returned results can occupy model context, especially when many tools are exposed.
options.D: MCP automatically doubles output length whenever more than ten tools are installed.

questions.question: A manager rejects an AI-generated customer response during an approval step. What should a properly designed workflow allow?

options.A: Permanently disable every future execution of the workflow.
options.B: Send the rejected message because AI generated it first.
options.C: Delete the customer's original request automatically.
options.D: Stop the send action or route the item for revision or manual handling.

questions.question: Keyword rules incorrectly route messages such as “I've been charged twice and need this fixed” because the exact word “refund” does not appear. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Add more Schedule Triggers.
options.B: Store every possible customer sentence as a fixed variable.
options.C: Use an LLM node to interpret the meaning and classify the message.
options.D: Use a loop until the word “refund” appears.

questions.question: A workflow receives a different customer name during every execution. The email node needs to insert that name automatically instead of using fixed text. Which n8n concept best supports this?

options.A: Docker images
options.B: Credentials
options.C: Trigger types
options.D: Expressions that reference changing workflow data

questions.question: A workflow receives invoices written in different layouts. The AI node must identify the supplier, invoice date, and total amount so those values can be stored in a database. Which AI capability is most relevant?

options.A: Credential creation
options.B: Workflow scheduling
options.C: Content generation
options.D: Information extraction

questions.question: A customer's order ID changes on every workflow execution. A confirmation message must always include the order ID returned by the previous node. What design is strongest?

options.A: Reference the previous node's order ID dynamically with an expression.
options.B: Store one example order ID in the authentication credential.
options.C: Ask an employee to edit the message before each execution.
options.D: Create a separate workflow for every order.

questions.question: A manager wants a reporting workflow to run automatically every morning and every evening. Which feature should primarily control those execution times?

options.A: Scheduling or an appropriate CRON configuration
options.B: Merge logic
options.C: Prompt templates
options.D: Credentials

questions.question: Two different branches of an n8n workflow retrieve related records that need to be combined before the next step. Which n8n component is specifically designed for this?

options.A: Manual Trigger
options.B: Schedule Trigger
options.C: Merge node
options.D: OAuth credential

questions.question: Docker Desktop shows that the n8n image exists, but no container can be started because the component responsible for running and managing containers is unavailable. Which component should be checked first?

options.A: n8n Workflow Editor
options.B: Docker Engine
options.C: n8n Execution History
options.D: Docker Volume

questions.question: A company designs the following process: AI evaluates a proposed record change → Human reviews → Approved changes continue; rejected changes do not. Which principle does this workflow illustrate?

options.A: Human approval is useful only for emails.
options.B: The workflow should always perform the action before review.
options.C: AI recommends a human review, and the workflow acts only after the decision.
options.D: The human should perform the AI analysis instead.

questions.question: During development, a trainee wants a workflow to run only when they deliberately click Execute so they can inspect every step. Which trigger is most suitable?

options.A: Manual Trigger
options.B: Form Trigger
options.C: Webhook Trigger
options.D: Schedule Trigger

questions.question: A trainee wants n8n to work with their Google account without storing their Google password in n8n. They sign in to Google, review requested permissions, and approve access. Which authentication approach does this describe?

options.A: Manual authentication
options.B: OAuth 2.0
options.C: Webhook authentication
options.D: API Key

questions.question: An HR workflow receives 150 applications. The same extraction and processing steps should run for each application without creating 150 copies of the workflow. What is the best design?

options.A: Use a loop to repeat the required steps for the applications.
options.B: Create one trigger per applicant.
options.C: Create one credential per applicant.
options.D: Merge all applications into one value and process them once.

questions.question: A support team processes thousands of messages with one standard AI classification workflow. The AI's role, categories, rules, and required output stay the same, while the customer message changes every execution. Which design is strongest?

options.A: Use a reusable prompt template containing fixed instructions and dynamic variables.
options.B: Write a new prompt manually for every incoming message.
options.C: Put the customer message inside the API key.
options.D: Store one example customer message permanently and use it for every execution.

questions.question: A prompt contains dynamic placeholders such as `Customer Name: {{ customer_name }}` and `Message: {{ customer_message }}` where surrounding instructions remain unchanged. What do these placeholders represent?

options.A: Trigger definitions
options.B: Dynamic data inserted by the workflow
options.C: Fixed instructions
options.D: Authentication secrets

questions.question: Consider this flow: Gmail → LLM Node → Classify Email → Google Sheets → Send Response. Why is this a connected flow?

options.A: All applications are running in one Docker container.
options.B: Multiple applications and workflow steps exchange and process data as part of one automated process.
options.C: Every node uses the same credential type.
options.D: The LLM performs every external action without the workflow.

questions.question: A new employee is added to the company's HR system. The organization wants accounts created, welcome information sent, required documents shared, and HR notified automatically. Which automation use case is this?

options.A: Research automation
options.B: Meeting-summary automation
options.C: Employee onboarding automation
options.D: Customer-support automation

questions.question: A workflow receives long meeting notes and must turn them into a short summary before the next step sends the result to a team channel. Which LLM-node capability is being used primarily?

options.A: Container management
options.B: Summarization
options.C: Authentication
options.D: Scheduling

questions.question: A Google-connected workflow only uses Drive and Sheets. During setup, a trainee suggests enabling Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Drive, and Sheets APIs “because we may need them someday.” What is the better approach?

options.A: Enable only the APIs required by the workflows that will actually use them.
options.B: Enable all Google APIs because OAuth cannot work with selected services.
options.C: Disable all APIs and place the Google password inside the workflow.
options.D: Create a new Google account for every individual node.

questions.question: A reusable automation prompt must tell the AI who it should act as, what to do, what information to consider, which changing values to insert, what restrictions to follow, and how to structure the answer. Which set best represents these components?

options.A: Image, Container, Engine, API, Webhook, Form
options.B: Input, Output, Docker, OAuth, CRON, Execution
options.C: Trigger, Node, Container, Loop, Schedule, Credential
options.D: Role, Task, Context, Variables, Rules, Output Format

questions.question: A workflow retrieves a list of 100 customers and must send each customer an individually addressed reminder. What is the strongest workflow design?

options.A: Create 100 separate OAuth credentials.
options.B: Loop through the customer items and use changing data in the reminder step.
options.C: Use one fixed email address for all executions.
options.D: Create 100 Docker containers.
